vocabulary.meaning: A field report of a problem at a location on the state highway system: D/C/R/PM + coordinates + first observed + media. It is an event attached to a location object; several incidents can accrue on one location (docs/WORKFLOWS_VERIFIED.md:71-75).
vocabulary.confusionRisk: Medium - a newcomer expects 'incident' to be the whole case; in ERIS the technical work is a separate Assessment. Mobile relabels it 'Case' for office/branch chiefs (mobile incidents/index.tsx:1884).

vocabulary.meaning: Web name for the shared grouping context across independent incidents at a location/event; created or chosen at coordinator triage; Mission Center drills statewide Event Groups -> incidents -> GIS evidence (web/src/pages/EventGroupsPage.tsx:26; MissionCenterProjectGisMap.tsx:111).
vocabulary.confusionRisk: High - the mobile triage flow and the web cross-section save dialog call the same object a 'Project' (mobile incidents/index.tsx:1300; CrossSectionSaveDialog.tsx:135), and the API fields are event_group_id / event_group_key while the map code still says project_id (MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:32-57).

vocabulary.meaning: Legacy / mobile synonym for Event Group; also the container a Terrain Cross Section is saved to.
vocabulary.confusionRisk: High - reads as a capital construction project to Caltrans staff, which it is not.

vocabulary.meaning: Canonical first-class location object a coordinator links an incident to (mode EXISTING or CREATE_NEW); the incident's history timeline is queryable from it (docs/WORKFLOWS_VERIFIED.md:77-87).
vocabulary.confusionRisk: Medium - overlaps conceptually with Event Group; both are 'the thing several incidents attach to'.

vocabulary.meaning: The incident's durable identifier minted when the coordinator accepts the report into ERIS; an Event Group member without one is a data-integrity error (EventGroupDetailPage.tsx:33-34, 103).
vocabulary.confusionRisk: High - never explained in UI; users will not know a report before triage has only a provisional identity.

vocabulary.meaning: Web /incidents tabs: reports not yet triaged ('not yet part of the record') vs coordinator-accepted reports (IncidentsOperationsPage.tsx:48-49).
vocabulary.confusionRisk: Medium - 'intake' is not used on mobile, which shows 'Under Review' instead.

vocabulary.meaning: The official product concept: the workflow wrapper (assessments table) for the technical work product after a report is accepted; states PENDING_OFFICE_DELEGATION -> PENDING_ENGINEER_ASSIGNMENT -> DRAFT -> SUBMITTED -> (REVISION_REQUESTED) -> APPROVED -> FINALIZED (assessments.py:70-77; docs/assessment-routing-authority-model.md:62-72).
vocabulary.confusionRisk: High - the mobile GISA form also has a step literally named 'Assessment' among Header / GISA Body / Assessment / Actions / Gallery (mobile submissions/[id].tsx:2781), so 'Assessment' means both the case wrapper and one section of the form.

vocabulary.meaning: The deep engineering form the engineer fills in (legacy GISA); stored in submissions + submission_gisa*; an assessment may have multiple technical submissions (docs/CLIENTS_VERIFIED.md:11, 23).
vocabulary.confusionRisk: High - web calls it 'submission', mobile has 'Drafts' and 'Submissions' tabs and 'Open Linked Draft #N', older docs say 'GISA draft'.

vocabulary.meaning: The legacy record for the technical form with its own status DRAFT -> SUBMITTED -> APPROVED / REJECTED and workflow_events audit (docs/WORKFLOWS_VERIFIED.md:10-20).
vocabulary.confusionRisk: High - 'submitted' is both a submission status and an assessment state, and mobile's 'Submissions' tab is really the technical-form list; web has no Submissions nav item at all.

vocabulary.meaning: Legacy name of the technical form (Geotechnical ... assessment); survives in table names, mobile section titles ('GISA Header', 'GISA Body', 'Generate GISA PDF') and the PDF template; intentionally not renamed (docs/assessment-routing-authority-model.md:14-37).
vocabulary.confusionRisk: High - the web is supposed to never say GISA (docs/incident-workflow-tree.md:21-23) while mobile says it constantly.

vocabulary.meaning: Either an assessment in state DRAFT (engineer working) or a submission with status DRAFT, or a mobile local offline draft (localDrafts.ts).
vocabulary.confusionRisk: High - three different 'drafts'.

vocabulary.meaning: The coordinator's single decision point on a report in COORDINATOR_REVIEW; records a disposition and, for ASSESSMENT_REQUIRED, creates the Assessment and routes it to a GeoTech office (assessments.py:363-408).
vocabulary.confusionRisk: Low-medium - 'Start triage' on web; older mobile / QA wording says 'Forward to Office Chief' (docs/field-workflow-qa.md:80-82).

vocabulary.meaning: One of four triage outcomes: ASSESSMENT_REQUIRED, NO_ASSESSMENT_REQUIRED, NEEDS_REPORTER_INFORMATION, DUPLICATE_OR_LINKED (assessments.py:391-398).
vocabulary.confusionRisk: Medium - 'disposition' is also the label on the workflow-tree terminal node ('No assessment required', 'Linked / duplicate report').

vocabulary.term: Needs reporter information / Needs Revision / Revision requested
vocabulary.meaning: Two different loops: NEEDS_REPORTER_INFORMATION sets the incident's location_match_status = NEEDS_REVISION and the reporter sees 'Needs Revision'; REVISION_REQUESTED is the assessment state when a reviewer returns the engineer's form.
vocabulary.confusionRisk: High - same word family for the reporter loop and the engineer loop; web's submission header says 'Return for correction' for the engineer loop.

vocabulary.meaning: Terminal triage disposition that closes the report and records duplicate_of_incident_id / duplicate_of_location_id; records are linked, not merged (docs/assessment-routing-authority-model.md:282-284).
vocabulary.confusionRisk: Medium - users may think the report is deleted.

vocabulary.meaning: Coordinator step: GET nearby candidates then POST location-link with EXISTING + location_id or CREATE_NEW; forward / triage is blocked until done (incidents.py:1227-1311).
vocabulary.confusionRisk: Medium - mobile phrases it as choosing a Project.

vocabulary.meaning: District -> GeoTech office mapping (NORTH / SOUTH / WEST) from geotech_office_routing with legacy fallback; the coordinator can preview and override with a reason (incidents.py:44-47; docs/assessment-routing-authority-model.md:152-166).
vocabulary.confusionRisk: High - 'Route' also means the highway route number in D/C/R/PM, and 'routing assignments' (/incidents/routing/assignments) means which users are district coordinators / office chiefs.

vocabulary.meaning: Office chief hands an assessment to a branch chief (POST delegate-branch), optionally naming the engineer at the same time.
vocabulary.confusionRisk: Low-medium - on mobile the label is 'Delegate to branch chief', on web just 'Delegate'.

vocabulary.meaning: Branch chief attaches the working engineer; creates the ENGINEER assessment assignment and the linked technical-form draft.
vocabulary.confusionRisk: Low - but mobile asks for a raw 'Engineer user id' text input.

vocabulary.meaning: Assessment-level assignment roles; only active REVIEWER / APPROVER assignments may review; CONSULTED is informational (docs/assessment-routing-authority-model.md:136-149).
vocabulary.confusionRisk: High - the legacy global REVIEWER role still exists and unlocks mobile Drafts / Submissions tabs, but does NOT grant review authority.

vocabulary.term: Approve / Return for correction / Request revision
vocabulary.meaning: Reviewer decisions on a SUBMITTED assessment: APPROVE -> APPROVED, REQUEST_REVISION -> REVISION_REQUESTED (assessments.py:1408-1441).
vocabulary.confusionRisk: Medium - the same action is 'Return for correction' on the web submission header and 'Request revision' on the assessment panel and mobile.

vocabulary.meaning: Office chief closes an APPROVED assessment (FINALIZED). Does not resolve the incident (open policy; docs/assessment-routing-authority-model.md:270-272).
vocabulary.confusionRisk: High - users will assume Finalized = case closed; the incident stays open until someone clicks Resolve.

vocabulary.meaning: Legacy incident close (status RESOLVED, current_stage RESOLVED) by engineer / admin, also used by NO_ASSESSMENT_REQUIRED and DUPLICATE_OR_LINKED triage.
vocabulary.confusionRisk: Medium - resolved can mean 'dismissed at triage' or 'assessment finalized and closed'.

vocabulary.meaning: Three parallel machines: incident status (NEW / IN_PROGRESS / RESOLVED), incident current_stage (COORDINATOR_REVIEW / OFFICE_CHIEF_REVIEW / BRANCH_CHIEF_REVIEW / ENGINEER_ASSIGNED / RESOLVED), assessment state (7 values), plus submission status and location_match_status (docs/WORKFLOWS_VERIFIED.md:26-29; assessments.py:70-77).
vocabulary.confusionRisk: Very high - mobile shows raw current_stage text ('Stage: OFFICE_CHIEF_REVIEW') to non-maintenance users (mobile incidents/index.tsx:1913) while web shows friendly assessment-state labels (roleModel.ts:81-93).

vocabulary.meaning: Web single queue of workflow steps waiting on the signed-in role; all action buttons live here, the record pages are read-only (docs/CLIENTS_VERIFIED.md:9-13; MyWorkPage.tsx:24-32).
vocabulary.confusionRisk: Low on web; no mobile equivalent - mobile puts actions inline on Track Incidents and Assessments.

vocabulary.meaning: Web statewide GIS view: Event Groups -> group incidents -> incident evidence with camera-heading wedges; deep-linkable (docs/CLIENTS_VERIFIED.md:15-17).
vocabulary.confusionRisk: Medium - sounds like a command post / dispatch tool; it is a read-only map explorer. Mobile tab was removed but native bridge remains (docs/CLIENTS_VERIFIED.md:55, 85).

vocabulary.meaning: Derived read model showing each incident's nodes (REPORTER_SUBMISSION ... RESOLUTION) with statuses COMPLETED / CURRENT / PENDING / WAITING_ON_REPORTER / REVISION_REQUESTED / SKIPPED / TERMINAL / UNASSIGNED and who owns the next action (docs/incident-workflow-tree.md:81-155).
vocabulary.confusionRisk: Low-medium - UNASSIGNED means 'a role but no person', which reads like an error.

vocabulary.meaning: GIS tool: draw a path, get a DEM elevation profile, export north-up aerial capture with P1..Pn points, save to a Project (web/src/features/terrainCrossSections/*).
vocabulary.confusionRisk: Medium - distinct from the road cross-section 'measurement diagram' inside the GISA form (docs/field-workflow-qa.md:107-113) and from the 3D Terrain scene on the submission page.

vocabulary.meaning: Caltrans linear reference along a route within a county (e.g. 0.17); required on every incident; normalised by normalize_post_mile (incidents.py:1138).
vocabulary.confusionRisk: Low for Caltrans staff, high for outsiders; mobile shows 'PM ?' when missing.

vocabulary.meaning: District / County / Route / Post Mile - the Caltrans location key stored verbatim on incidents and submissions (docs/CLIENTS_VERIFIED.md:34; incidents.py:1141-1144). County is a 3-letter code such as ORA; district is a number such as 12.
vocabulary.confusionRisk: Medium - 'Route' collides with office routing; 'District' is a maintenance district, not a GeoTech office.

vocabulary.term: Road Inventory / RI context / Dataset / Segment
vocabulary.meaning: Admin-published XLSX roadway dataset, packaged for offline mobile use; the incident form matches D/C/R/PM to a segment and snapshots lanes / surface; the snapshot drives the GISA measurement diagram (docs/field-workflow-qa.md:1-56, 93-113).
vocabulary.confusionRisk: Medium - 'RI context saved · Dataset X · Seg Y' is jargon on the reporter's list.

vocabulary.meaning: Generated offline bundle of the published road-inventory version with size, date and SHA-256 (docs/field-workflow-qa.md:19-24).
vocabulary.confusionRisk: Medium - could be mistaken for an app update.

vocabulary.term: Measurements / Failure side (LT / RT / Both) / Template (Landslide, Cut-slope)
vocabulary.meaning: GISA form section with the roadway cross-section diagram; failure side and template change overlays (docs/field-workflow-qa.md:107-113).
vocabulary.confusionRisk: Low for engineers; hidden from other roles.

vocabulary.meaning: Map glyph showing which direction a field photo was taken (docs/CLIENTS_VERIFIED.md:16, 35).
vocabulary.confusionRisk: Low.

vocabulary.meaning: Web attachment browser (Photos / Videos / Documents chips) and the /submissions/:id/photo-evidence deep link; mobile calls it 'Gallery'.
vocabulary.confusionRisk: Medium - three names for attachments.

vocabulary.meaning: Legacy endpoint POST /incidents/{id}/claim, now returns a disabled error (docs/WORKFLOWS_VERIFIED.md:43; incidents.py:1636).
vocabulary.confusionRisk: Low - should not appear in UI.

vocabulary.meaning: Legacy role code FIELD_WORKER = the GeoTech ENGINEER, whereas 'Maintenance Field Worker' = the reporter (backend/app/roles.py:5-6; docs/assessment-routing-authority-model.md:97-99).
vocabulary.confusionRisk: Very high - the plain-English meaning is the opposite of the code; user role chips in the web header show raw codes (AppShell.tsx:157).

vocabulary.meaning: Legacy role code for the maintenance field reporter; also the Caltrans division that files reports.
vocabulary.confusionRisk: Medium.

vocabulary.meaning: Any non-maintenance role (coordinator, chiefs, engineer, legacy reviewer, admin) with broad read access to all incidents / assessments (roles.py:64-70, 101-103).
vocabulary.confusionRisk: Low - internal term, but it gates nav visibility.

vocabulary.meaning: Query flag making the backend filter incidents by role (own / district / office / assigned) for the mobile app (docs/APP_DEEP_DIVE.md:147-154).
vocabulary.confusionRisk: Low - invisible to users, but explains why mobile and web lists differ.

vocabulary.meaning: Mobile persisted operation queue replayed in order when online; stops at first failure with attempt count (docs/WORKFLOWS_VERIFIED.md:107-113).
vocabulary.confusionRisk: Medium - a stuck first op silently blocks everything behind it.

vocabulary.meaning: Mobile ArcGIS native sketch flow for drawing on a map within the form (docs/CLIENTS_VERIFIED.md:83-84).
vocabulary.confusionRisk: Low.

vocabulary.meaning: The old /submissions list page kept on web without a nav item (docs/CLIENTS_VERIFIED.md:26-27).
vocabulary.confusionRisk: Medium - reachable by URL, duplicates the Assessments view with older vocabulary.

notes: Mobile vs web naming of the same thing: Event Group (web) = Project (mobile triage prompt at mobile/app/(tabs)/incidents/index.tsx:1300 and web cross-section save dialog); Incident (web, mobile for reporters) = Case (mobile for office/branch chiefs, incidents/index.tsx:1884); technical submission (web Assessments) = Drafts / Submissions tabs + 'Open Linked Draft #N' + 'GISA' (mobile); Request revision (web panel, mobile) = Return for correction (web submission header); Start triage (web) = four-disposition triage picker on Track Incidents (mobile) = 'Forward to Office Chief' (older QA doc / legacy coordinator/forward endpoint); Gallery (mobile) = Submission library / Photo evidence (web); friendly assessment-state labels (web roleModel.ts:81-93) vs raw current_stage codes (mobile incidents/index.tsx:1913) vs 'Under Review' / 'Needs Revision' badges for reporters.

Web is action-centric through My Work with read-only record pages (Incidents page has no workflow buttons); mobile has no My Work and puts actions inline on Track Incidents and Assessments, with free-text user-id inputs for delegate / assign (docs/assessment-routing-authority-model.md:303-305).

Role-code hazard: legacy FIELD_WORKER means the GeoTech engineer and legacy MAINTENANCE means the reporter; the web header shows raw role codes joined by ' · ' (AppShell.tsx:157). Any UI that echoes role codes will mislead newcomers.

Mobile tab gating uses legacy codes only (MAINTENANCE, FIELD_WORKER, MAINT_COORDINATOR, OFFICE_CHIEF, BRANCH_CHIEF, REVIEWER, ADMIN) except the Assessments tab, which uses isOperationalUser; a user seeded only with canonical roles would lose Create Incident / Drafts / Submissions tabs (mobile/app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx:46-61). ADMIN is treated as a maintenance worker on mobile (Create Incident tab).

Reviewer is an assessment-level assignment, not a job role; the legacy global REVIEWER role still unlocks mobile tabs but grants no review authority (roles.py:23-27; assessments.py:1398-1403). The reviewer persona above is therefore usually a chief or senior engineer wearing a second hat.

Three parallel status vocabularies (incident status, incident current_stage, assessment state) plus submission status and location_match_status are all shown somewhere; the Assessment endpoints keep the legacy stage machine in sync (docs/assessment-routing-authority-model.md:74-77).

Open policy: FINALIZED does not auto-resolve the incident; the workflow tree shows RESOLUTION as CURRENT owned by the engineer until someone calls /incidents/{id}/resolve (docs/incident-workflow-tree.md:179-183). One assessment per incident is enforced (uk_assessment_incident); triage is a single decision point only in COORDINATOR_REVIEW.

Coordinator is auto-assigned by district via DISTRICT_COORDINATOR routing at incident creation; if no routing row exists the report sits UNASSIGNED with no notification (incidents.py:1198-1218), which is an admin-facing failure mode.

Web nav by persona (AppShell.tsx:79-102): reporter sees Incidents + Settings only; operational roles add My Work, Mission Center, Event Groups, Assessments, Terrain Cross Sections; admin adds Users and Road Inventory.

docs/field-workflow-qa.md predates the Assessment layer (uses 'GISA draft', 'Forward to Office Chief'); docs/assessment-routing-authority-model.md and docs/incident-workflow-tree.md are the current source of truth and explicitly forbid 'GISA' in new user-facing text.
